recommended_title: Protected Reporting After Prompt Selection: Benefits and Limits
central_question: When does reserving benchmark questions for reporting reduce error after prompt selection, and what can known-truth simulations versus finite real-model audits establish about reliability?
central_thesis: Across the five final seeds, half-split reporting lowers mean error relative to reusing the same winner's selection score in the sixteen-prompt conditions, but does not uniformly beat full-budget or non-search comparators, and the real-model results establish audit agreement rather than population validity.
narrative_rationale: The strongest evidence is a controlled study of a retained, conventional reporting policy, not an improved optimizer or a new inference method. Known-truth synthetic conditions isolate selection optimism and the cost of withholding observations; a small real instruction model supplies a bounded empirical check with explicit audit uncertainty. The final evaluation is independently completed and qualified, even though the search found no qualifying replacement and all three candidate attempts were unscored. Method novelty, universal superiority, and reliable fresh-population coverage are not supported. A standalone empirical-methodology paper is coherent if it leads with the comparison and keeps these counterexamples and limitations in the main text.
edit_framing_decision: No previous_paper directory, resolved edit-context file, aggregated directory, or extra_tasks directory is present; this is fresh framing, not a manuscript-preservation decision. The recentered label denotes a move from the task's broad automatic-tuning ambition and private proposal history to the frozen baseline's measured reporting trade-off. There is no prior manuscript title or figure plan to preserve.
staged_input_impact: The staged selected and baseline source files are byte-identical and implement a frozen sixteen-prompt bank, seeded random half selection/half reporting, uniform reporting weights, and fixed tie priority. This rules out treating their comparison as an intervention or gain.

study.selection_kind, study.investigation_outcome, study.search_score_delta, and study.attempts.* establish baseline retention, no qualifying search replacement, zero search-score delta, zero scored attempts, and three unscored attempts. The missing scores are not losses.

final.qualification.status/outcome/correct independently establish completed/qualified/true. final.evidence.episodes contains five seeds and eight conditions per seed; this final evidence, not the search outcome, enables the paper.

The staged task/evaluate_final.py SHA256 exactly matches final_evaluation.evaluator_sha256. Its estimator, controls, bootstrap target, synthetic construction, and aggregation therefore have direct evaluator linkage rather than speculative family linkage.

The runtime and split manifests identify CPU float32 SmolLM2-135M-Instruct with deterministic one-letter constrained decoding and pinned MMLU-Pro. They narrow the real evidence to one small model and one public benchmark, not arbitrary LLM pipelines.

The retained episode details mark candidate diagnostics unverified. Intentional contaminated-copy independence flags must be explained as negative controls, not mistaken for the actual policy failing final qualification; they also cannot establish general validity or adaptivity robustness.

method_groups.name: Protected half-split reporting
method_groups.include_reason: Central studied policy: select the highest-accuracy prompt on one random half and report its uniform accuracy with a 95% Wilson interval on the disjoint half. It is the retained baseline, not a newly invented estimator.

method_groups.name: Same-winner selection-score reuse
method_groups.include_reason: Primary matched comparison: the selected prompt is identical to that of protected reporting, isolating the reporting sample rather than a different winner. Do not call this full-benchmark reuse.

method_groups.name: Full-budget selection and reuse
method_groups.include_reason: Select and report on all available benchmark questions. This uses a different winner and more reporting observations, exposing the bias-variance and selection-budget trade-off rather than providing a pure reporting ablation.

method_groups.name: Fixed and random prompt reporting
method_groups.include_reason: Non-search reference points with full-question reporting; each error is evaluated against that method's own prompt target. They can have lower reporting MSE without selecting a better prompt. Include in the main numerical table, not as extra series in crowded plots.

method_groups.name: Alternative half-split and diagnostic controls
method_groups.include_reason: The evaluator's first-half/second-half comparator is another half-split implementation, not a distinct statistical advance. Constant outputs, copied arms, deliberately contaminated reporting, permutation, and replay check protocol behavior. Explain their limited roles; they are not outcome-adaptive methods or proof of population validity.

results_focus: Separate the scientific condition grid from campaign history: synthetic versus real evidence, total question budget n in {64,256}, and prompt count K in {1,16}, each over five final seeds. Synthetic details contain four regimes with 1024 replicates each; real details contain one benchmark/audit realization per seed and condition, not 1024 independent model runs.

Lead with condition-specific protected-report, same-winner-reuse, and full-budget-reuse error comparisons. Use the single-prompt condition as a no-selection diagnostic: splitting still costs observations. Keep the synthetic full-budget advantage visible rather than asserting that reduced optimism guarantees lower MSE.

Use the supplied aggregate only as secondary context: final.metric.report_mse=0.0033498776393466522 versus final.metric.reuse_mse=0.005354862639043066, but final.metric.full_budget_naive_mse=0.002705803510381116 and final.metric.fixed_prompt_mse=0.0021956944465637207 are lower. Do not conflate this mixed-family average with population risk or a single dataset result.

Explain synthetic optimism using equal versus graded arm means and shared-outcome mixing parameters 0.1 versus 0.9; the latter is the generator's dependence parameter, not an asserted exact Pearson correlation. Use regime-wise bias, MSE, Wilson coverage and width from episode details. Known truth supports simulation coverage statements, not a new coverage theorem.

For real data, report error relative to a 512-question audit and selected-minus-fixed audit accuracy with the retained paired subject-bootstrap intervals. These intervals concern the accuracy difference, not reporting bias or the MSE difference. Do not portray whether a Wilson interval contains an audit estimate as known population coverage.

Make the lack of stable real-model superiority explicit: the retained sixteen-prompt audit intervals have mixed signs/zero inclusion, and the conditions share a public data pool. Show every final seed, not only intervals above zero. Do not pool these correlated intervals into an unqualified significance claim.

Keep source-qualified status separate from scientific conclusions: final.qualification.* reports a qualified completed evaluation; study.* reports no scored candidate improvement. Missing detailed gate diagnostics and unverified candidate diagnostics remain limitations despite that status.
figure_plan: Figure 1, early conceptual overview: frozen prompt bank, random selection/report split, same-winner reuse alternative, and separate synthetic-known-truth versus finite-real-audit targets; mark full-budget selection as a different winner/comparison.

Figure 2, main direct comparison: a two-by-two condition grid, with rows synthetic/real and columns n=64/256, two K categories and three reporting series; overlay five seed-level observations and distinguish population MSE from audit-reference squared error in the row labels.

Figure 3, real uncertainty: two horizontal interval panels for n=64/256, displaying selected-minus-fixed audit accuracy for all five final seeds at K=16, with zero reference and retained paired subject-bootstrap intervals.

figure_specs.purpose: Give immediate glance value for the estimand, protected sample, same-winner comparator, and unequal evidential strength of known truth and finite audit.
figure_specs.metric: none; conceptual evidence and data-flow map
figure_specs.split_by: selection/report data roles and synthetic/real targets
figure_specs.layout_rationale: paper.sty sets a single 5.5-inch text column and 9-inch text height. Use that full 5.5-inch span on page 1 or 2, approximately 1.6 inches high plus caption (about one fifth page), with at least 9-point final labels. A half-width inset would compress branching data roles; there is no two-column figure* assumption.
figure_specs.implementation_notes: At most six semantic blocks, short node labels, no numerical result decorations, no invented model architecture or adaptive feedback loop. Describe selection/report independence as the intended random-partition design, not an evaluator-certified population property. Require editable draw.io output and regenerate rather than shrink if text exceeds budget.

figure_specs.purpose: Compare error while keeping sample size, prompt count, target type, and the strongest counterexample to uniform superiority visible.
figure_specs.metric: synthetic: mean squared error to known selected-prompt accuracy; real: squared discrepancy to audit accuracy
figure_specs.split_by: synthetic versus real and n=64 versus n=256
figure_specs.layout_rationale: Use 5.5 inches by approximately 2.8 inches plus caption, a 2x2 grid with only two x categories and three series per panel. A single legend and at least 8.5-point rendered labels keep it readable at full text width; half-width is unsuitable. Reserve about two fifths page. Use matched scales within each evidence row or explicitly label any row-specific scale; do not imply identical targets across rows.
figure_specs.implementation_notes: Three series: protected report, selection-score reuse, full-budget reuse. Overlay seed points within those series rather than adding seed legend entries. Means are descriptive across the five retained seeds, with synthetic regimes equally weighted. Do not invent paired-difference standard errors from marginal MSE standard errors; display seed scatter instead. Use a table for the remaining comparators.

figure_specs.purpose: Prevent improved reporting from being mistaken for improved selected-prompt accuracy and expose finite-audit uncertainty.
figure_specs.metric: selected minus fixed prompt audit accuracy, with paired subject-bootstrap 95% percentile interval
figure_specs.layout_rationale: Use a 5.5-inch-wide two-panel plot approximately 1.8 inches high plus caption (roughly one quarter page), five horizontal seed rows per panel and one interval series. Keep at least 8.5-point labels, shared x limits, and a zero line. Full-width avoids squeezing signed accuracy labels into a narrow inset; in this single-column style full-width equals column width.
figure_specs.implementation_notes: Point estimates equal detail.target minus detail.fixed[1]; endpoints are detail.paired_subject_bootstrap_interval. All five seeds must appear. The evaluator uses 200 subject-cluster bootstrap draws, and these intervals are not simultaneous or a validation of the bootstrap procedure. K=1 yields the identical prompt and is tabulated rather than using a redundant panel.

supplementary_plan.purpose: Provide full condition and regime accountability, exact statistical semantics, and reproducibility beyond the main comparison, without relocating the central counterexamples or essential validity limitations out of the body.

planned_subsections.heading: Complete Condition and Regime Results
planned_subsections.grounded_content: Tabulate all eight conditions for each of the five final seeds, all six reporting comparators, selected accuracy, report bias, reuse optimism, interval width, and coverage indicators. Expand synthetic results into four regimes per condition using the retained metrics and report-MSE standard errors. Separate real audit-containment indicators from synthetic population coverage; do not estimate unobserved replicate distributions.

planned_subsections.heading: Partition, Estimand, and Uncertainty Details
planned_subsections.grounded_content: Specify frozen prompt texts and tie order, seeded half partition, the evaluator's alternative half split, Wilson interval calculation, own-winner targets for differing selection methods, synthetic shared-uniform generator and arm means, equal weighting, and the 200-draw subject bootstrap for selected-minus-fixed audit accuracy. Ground definitions in the SHA256-matched task/evaluate_final.py and staged policy source; do not present these as newly proved inferential guarantees.

planned_subsections.heading: Diagnostic Controls and Evidence Boundaries
planned_subsections.grounded_content: Document constant, copy-arm, deliberately contaminated copy-report, effective permutation, and replay observations. Explain why the contaminated control records independence=false while final qualification is qualified. State that candidate diagnostics are unverified and unknown gate checks cannot be inferred. Describe the unmatched program-tree hash scopes without asserting identity across those scopes; selected versus baseline local source equality is directly established.

planned_subsections.heading: Reproducibility, Resources, and Incomplete Comparisons
planned_subsections.grounded_content: Record model and dataset revisions from task/resources/final/runtime_manifest.json and split_manifest.json, CPU precision, constrained decoding, context exclusions, dependencies from task/requirements.txt, seed list and evaluator command flags. Include per-seed observed durations from final evidence, distinguishing elapsed evaluator time from unrecorded CPU-hours, inference calls, and tokens. Give future reproduction/table/figure generation commands as instructions, not already executed experiments. Transparently note the retained baseline, three unscored search attempts, and absent scored ablations; do not narrate speculative reasons for timeouts or call them measured losses.

planned_subsections.heading: LLM Usage
planned_subsections.grounded_content: Disclose task-observed LLM assistance in research ideation, policy implementation, reference planning, and manuscript framing/writing separately from the evaluated model's benchmark-answer generation. Precisely distinguish retained evidence from proposals and do not infer undocumented human oversight or verification. This is mandatory under VENUE.md and must not contain author-identifying paths or internal service names.

notes_for_writer: Ground quantitative claims in final.metric.* or final.evidence.episodes, qualification in final.qualification.*, and selection, search differences, and attempt accounting in study.*. Never substitute downstream_study.final_evaluation for the independent final record. If authoritative qualification changes to not_qualified, disclose it in the body, review, audit and revision; identify a cause only if evaluator evidence establishes it. The current source says qualified, not failed.

Private-only pipeline context: the retained search score equals its baseline score and has zero delta; these are not accuracy measurements or final-scope improvements. Do not put those internal score labels into visible figures. The baseline is the studied policy; do not manufacture a second identical baseline series.

Problem formalization should distinguish a prompt selected from a frozen bank, its conditional fresh-question accuracy, the reused selection mean, the protected report mean, and the finite audit estimate. Reporting MSE and selected-prompt accuracy answer different questions. Full-budget, fixed, random, and alternative-half methods have their own prompt targets, so their MSE differences do not isolate a single mechanism.

The real setting is HuggingFaceTB/SmolLM2-135M-Instruct revision 12fd25f77366fa6b3b4b768ec3050bf629380bac on MMLU-Pro revision b189ec765aa7ed75c8acfea42df31fdae71f97be, CPU float32, deterministic constrained one-letter generation. Do not replace it with an assumed 7B model, chain-of-thought optimizer, DSPy implementation, or free-form response task. Public-data pretraining contamination is possible, not established.

The four synthetic regimes cross equal/graded means and shared-outcome dependence; one prompt has no selection multiplicity. All source-defined conditions remain visible. The cross-family aggregate uses equal case/seed/regime weights rather than pooling synthetic replicates with real examples. Derive any display summaries reproducibly from paper_data.json and label weighting explicitly; do not introduce ungrounded numeric confidence intervals.

Observed control completion, zero replay discrepancy, and qualified status do not imply representative sampling, verified candidate diagnostics, adaptation-safe inference, or reliable repeated-population coverage. The copy-report control is deliberately contaminated and correctly records false independence. The decision-reversal metric uses protected-report-minus-full-sample-fixed versus selected-target-minus-fixed-target signs, excludes ties, and is not the probability that a naive claim is overturned; omit it from the main story unless its exact estimand is explained.

Use one common research question with separate evidential roles: known-truth simulation for bias/coverage and real inference for finite-audit agreement and prompt-accuracy uncertainty. Do not merge them into a single population coverage headline. Real audit pools overlap across settings and derive from a shared public pool; seed scatter is descriptive, not evidence for independent datasets or repeated training runs.

Body target is 8.5 pages within VENUE.md's 8-9-page limit, excluding references: 1.25 pages for title/abstract/problem/contributions and the early overview; 0.75 related work; 1.5 estimands and reporting policies; 1.0 design/provenance; 2.0 controlled comparisons with Figure 2 and the all-comparator table; 0.75 real audit uncertainty with Figure 3; 1.25 interpretation, limitations, reproducibility pointer and conclusion. These are layout allocations, not measured results. A body of exactly 8 pages requires its last page at least 75% full. Spend space on target distinctions, regime-wise uncertainty and counterexamples rather than larger figures, repeated prose or new experiments.

Include a compact main table of all six comparators and a synthetic regime diagnostic table covering report bias, reuse optimism, coverage and interval width. The negative comparisons and finite-audit caveat remain in the body, not only the supplement.
